d: This episode of Tarikh explores the life of Aziz Mian, a qawwal who transformed the genre with his raw, confrontational style. Rising from Lahore’s shrines in the 1970s, he gained fame with Main Sharabi, blending Sufi thought with bold questions about faith and life. The story covers his rivalry with the Sabri Brothers, clashes with authority during Zia-ul-Haq’s regime, and the changing face of qawwali with Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan’s rise. More than music, it’s a tale of rebellion, devotion, and self-destruction — a man who challenged traditions and even argued with God through his art. Watch…
